security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates SSPUSH/C.SSPUSH as an atomic decrement-then-store sequence (old spec ordering), or serializes the ssp update and shadow-stack store with stronger ordering than the spec permits. In MTTCG mode, if SSPUSH is implemented as a single TCG helper that atomically updates ssp and performs the store without modeling the relaxed store/ssp-update ordering, QEMU enforces ordering guarantees that real RISC-V hardware does not provide.
security_spec.summary: QEMU TCG may implement SSPUSH with stronger-than-spec ordering (atomic decrement-then-store), hiding race conditions in guest CFI shadow-stack code that real hardware's relaxed store/ssp-update ordering would expose, enabling shadow-stack bypass exploits to go undetected during emulation-based testing

findings.finding: SSPUSH TCG translation emits the shadow-stack memory store (tcg_gen_qemu_st_tl, line 65-66) followed by the ssp CSR update (tcg_gen_st_tl, line 67) as sequential TCG ops within a single translation block. In MTTCG mode, other vCPUs observe both the store and the ssp update atomically with sequential consistency — there is no relaxed ordering between them. In real RISC-V hardware (RVWMO), the shadow-stack store and the ssp CSR update have relaxed ordering: another hart could observe the ssp update before the shadow-stack store becomes visible, or vice versa. QEMU TCG enforces strictly stronger ordering than real hardware permits, which can mask concurrency bugs that would manifest on silicon. Both the 32-bit SSPUSH (insn32.decode:1050-1051) and the compressed C.SSPUSH (insn16.decode:148) decode to this same trans_sspush function.

SSPOPCHK follows the inverse pattern of SSPUSH: it loads from the shadow-stack memory (tcg_gen_qemu_ld_tl, line 37-38), compares against rs1, and then increments ssp (tcg_gen_addi_tl + tcg_gen_st_tl, lines 47-48). The load and ssp-increment are sequentially ordered within the same TB. Per the updated spec with relaxed ordering, the ssp increment and the shadow-stack load should have relaxed ordering — another hart could observe the ssp increment before the load is visible. QEMU's sequential ordering is too strong.

CSR read handler for SSP returns env->ssp directly with no WARL masking or side effects. In the relaxed-ordering model, a read of ssp on another hart should be able to observe the updated ssp even if the corresponding shadow-stack store has not yet completed (or vice versa). QEMU's sequential consistency means reads always observe a fully-completed SSPUSH sequence, eliminating the relaxed-ordering race window that exists on real hardware.

CSR write handler for SSP directly stores val into env->ssp with no WARL masking or TLB/cache side effects. A direct CSR write to ssp (csrrw) has no ordering relationship with concurrent shadow-stack memory operations from SSPUSH/SSPOPCHK on other harts. In MTTCG, the write is instantaneously visible — real hardware would have relaxed visibility semantics.

VMState migration subsection for ssp serializes env.ssp as a plain UINTTL field. During live migration, ssp is captured at TB boundaries. While migration happens between TBs (not mid-instruction), there is no cross-field consistency validation between the migrated ssp value and shadow-stack memory contents on the destination side. If a source QEMU has an in-flight SSPUSH race (even if masked by QEMU's strong ordering), the destination has no way to detect inconsistency between ssp and shadow-stack memory.

Returns whether backward CFI (shadow stack) is enabled for the current privilege mode. Uses the correct privilege-level hierarchy (M-mode always enabled, S/U-mode require BCFI bit in corresponding *envcfg register). The function is structurally sound. It gates the BCFI_ENABLED TB flag that controls trans_sspush execution. No ordering-model issues introduced here.
CPU reset initializes ssp to 0, which is the architecturally-defined reset value per the Zicfiss spec. No ordering issues at reset — all harts start with ssp=0 before any SSPUSH execution begins.
findings.snippet:
/* on reset ssp is set to 0 */
env->ssp = 0;

findings.finding: TB flags computation sets BCFI_ENABLED based on cpu_get_bcfien(). The flag is per-TB and properly triggers TB flush on senvcfg changes via the envcfg write path. No ordering-model issues — this correctly controls instruction legality but does not participate in memory ordering.
